Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#1
Main.sentence: The Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets was a financial program announced on March 23, 2009, by the United States ___E:Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Deposit_Insurance_Corporation)___ (FDIC), the ___E:Federal Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve)___ , and the ___E:United States Treasury Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Treasury_Department)___ , designed to provide liquidity for so-called " ___E:toxic assets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxic_assets)___ " on the balance sheets of financial institutions.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#2
Main.sentence: It was one of the initiatives launched as part of the ___E:Troubled Asset Relief Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program)___ (TARP), as implemented by the U.S.

Main.sentence: The major stock market indexes in the United States rallied on the day of the announcement, rising by over six percent, with shares of bank stocks rising most.  As of early June 2009, the program had not yet been implemented, and was considered delayed.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#5
Main.sentence: The Legacy Securities Program implemented by the Federal Reserve had begun by the fall of 2009 and the Legacy Loans Program was being tested by the FDIC. The proposed size of the program was drastically reduced when rolled out, relative to its proposed size.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#6
Main.sentence: Using $75 to $100 billion in TARP capital and capital from private investors, the Public–Private Investment Program ( ___E:P-PIP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P-PIP)___ ) will generate $500 billion in purchasing power to buy legacy assets with the potential to expand to $1 trillion over time. Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#7
Main.sentence: PPIP uses a combination of private equity and Government equity and debt through TARP to facilitate purchases of legacy mortgage-backed securities ("MBS") held by financial institutions.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#8
Main.sentence: In July 2009, Treasury announced the selection of nine Public–Private Investment Fund ("PPIF") managers.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#9
Main.sentence: Treasury has obligated $21.9 billion in TARP funds to the program.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#10
Main.sentence: In January 2010, PPIP manager The TCW Group Inc. ("TCW") withdrew from the program.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#11
Main.sentence: On April 3, 2012, PPIP manager Invesco announced it had sold all remaining securities in its portfolio and was in the process of winding up the fund. The remaining seven PPIP managers are currently purchasing investments and managing their portfolios.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#12
Main.sentence: According to Treasury, the purpose of the Public–Private Investment Program ("PPIP") is to purchase legacy securities from banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, pension funds, and other eligible financial institutions as defined in EESA, through PPIFs.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#13
Main.sentence: PPIFs are partnerships, formed specifically for this program, that invest in mortgage-backed securities using equity capital from private-sector investors combined with TARP equity and debt. A private-sector fund management firm oversees each PPIF on behalf of these investors.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#14
Main.sentence: According to Treasury, the aim of PPIP was to "restart the market for legacy securities, allowing banks and other financial institutions to free up capital and stimulate the extension of new credit." PPIP originally included a Legacy Loans subprogram that would have involved purchases of troubled legacy loans with private and Treasury equity capital, as well as an FDIC guarantee for debt financing.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#15
Main.sentence: TARP funds were never disbursed for this subprogram.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#16
Main.sentence: Treasury selected nine fund management firms to establish PPIFs.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#17
Main.sentence: One PPIP manager, The TCW Group, Inc., ("TCW") subsequently withdrew, and another PPIP manager, Invesco, announced recently that it has sold all remaining securities in its PPIP fund. Private investors and Treasury co-invested in the PPIFs to purchase legacy securities from financial institutions.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#18
Main.sentence: The fund managers raised private-sector capital.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#19
Main.sentence: Treasury matched the private-sector equity dollar-for-dollar and provided debt financing in the amount of the total combined equity.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#20
Main.sentence: Each PPIP manager was also required to invest at least $20 million of its own money in the PPIF. Each PPIF is approximately 75% TARP funded.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#21
Main.sentence: PPIP was designed as an eight-year program.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#22
Main.sentence: PPIP managers have until 2017 to sell the assets in their portfolio.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#23
Main.sentence: Under certain circumstances, Treasury can terminate it early or extend it for up to two additional years.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#24
Main.sentence: Treasury, the PPIP managers, and the private investors share PPIF profits and losses on a pro rata basis based on their limited partnership interests.

Main.id: Public–Private Investment Program for Legacy Assets - Wikipedia#25
Main.sentence: Treasury also received warrants in each PPIF that give Treasury the right to receive a portion of the fund's profits that would otherwise be distributed to the private investors along with its pro rata share of program proceeds.

Main.sentence: In addition to the eligible securities, the PPIP portfolio also consists of cash assets to be used to purchase securities.
